A Fenway Instagram post has fans speculating about Noah Kahan’s summer tour plans.
 Print this Article 
 View Comments Noah Kahan arrived at the Emmy Awards last month wearing a bug pin. FREDERIC J. BROWN/AFP via Getty Images The US dates of Noah Kahan’s 2027 summer tour won’t be announced until tomorrow – or so we’ve heard – but it looks like the Vermont native will be coming back to Fenway Park. 
 The Instagram account FenwayConcerts was among several US venues that teased the singer’s tour itinerary Wednesday by posting an image of a bug. Kahan’s summer shows are being billed as “The Last of the Bugs” tour, a reference to a lyric in “ The View Between Villages ,” a song on the singer’s platinum-selling LP, “ The Great Divide .” 
 Kahan, who’s become one of the biggest musical acts in the world, performed four sold-out shows at Fenway Park in July. But many assumed he had outgrown the friendly confines of Fenway Park (capacity 36,000) and would instead play for more people – and substantially more money – at Gillette Stadium (capacity 56,000) next summer. 
 Get Starting Point A guide through the most important stories of the morning, delivered Monday through Friday. Enter Email Sign Up And he still may. The word among people involved in booking and promoting shows around Boston is that Fenway and Gillette had been vying to secure Kahan shows, and that negotiation could be ongoing. There was speculation that the singer might play several dates at Fenway and also a couple of nights at Gillette. 
 Noah Kahan waves to his fans while leaving his concert at Fenway Park on July 11, 2026. Christian Kantosky for The Boston Globe But of the venues teasing a Kahan tour stop online Wednesday, Fenway was the only baseball park. MetLife Stadium in New Jersey, Raymond James Stadium in Tampa Bay, Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas, Ford Field in Detroit, Bank of America Stadium in Charlotte, and Nissan Stadium in Nashville are all football stadiums, with vastly greater capacities than the home of the Red Sox. 
 If Kahan doesn’t play at Gillette Stadium next summer, some may wonder if it’s because of Robert Kraft. Last month, the Patriots owner demanded that rapper Macklemore be removed from Ed Sheeran’s show at Gillette for yelling “Free Palestine!” at a show in New Jersey. Although Kahan, once dubbed “ the Jewish Ed Sheeran ,” has not publicly commented on Kraft’s intervention, he was one of several artists who liked Macklemore’s statement on social media after he was kicked off Sheeran’s tour. 
 But if money is Kahan’s primary consideration, he would make more of it at Gillette Stadium, where artists can earn upwards of $7 million per sold-out show, depending on ticket prices. (Kahan would make about half that for a Fenway concert.) While some believe Kahan is popular enough to sell out at least four shows at Gillette, that would be a first in Foxborough. Only Taylor Swift and Kenny Chesney have played as many three nights at Gillette.
